## The notch, anywhere on your monitor
- **Move it along the top edge.** On an external monitor, press and hold the notch and slide it left or right. It snaps to the middle, and each monitor remembers its own spot. On a MacBook it stays on the camera, as before. - **See where it goes.** Settings → General now shows your displays as macOS arranges them, with the notch on the one it's shown on. Click a display to move it there, or drag the notch on a monitor. It glows for a moment so you can spot it. - **No more covering your tabs.** On a monitor the closed notch is now only as tall as the menu bar, so it no longer hangs over window tabs and title bars.
## Fixes
- Clicking a moved notch no longer opens the app menu behind it. - With the notch on a monitor of a different height, clicking outside the open panel now reaches the right spot.

## No more keychain prompts for Claude usage
macOS kept asking to let CrewNotch read "Claude Code-credentials", even after you chose Always Allow. Claude Code rewrites that keychain item every time it refreshes its sign-in, and each rewrite dropped CrewNotch's permission.
CrewNotch now reads the sign-in the same way Claude Code does, through the system's `security` tool. That tool is already allowed to read the item, so macOS doesn't ask and no new permission is granted. As before, the sign-in is only read, never changed.

## omux support
CrewNotch now recognizes [omux](https://github.com/onurozcan/omux) as a terminal.
- **Click a session to bring omux forward.** CrewNotch brings the omux window to the front. It can't pick the session's tab yet, because omux doesn't offer a way for other apps to do that. - **No sounds or notifications when you're already looking.** While omux is the frontmost app, CrewNotch treats its sessions like those in any other terminal and stays quiet. - Approving from the notch works in omux like everywhere else. If you answer in the notch, omux doesn't show its own prompt.
